title: Measuring carbonate dissolution rates under well-controlled conditions for reactive CO2-water flow in a large lab-scale karst fracture imitate
author: Strauch, Zimmer, et al.
materials: Each of the experimental runs was conducted with similar settings but with three different types of process-water. The water was supplied via containers (12 l volume) and taken fresh from a Millipore facility (Seralpur Pro 90CN) to ensure ion-free initial conditions (<0.05 µS/cm). This was used in the same way as for the experiments with CO2-free process water. When process water with 50 % CO2-saturation was applied for the experiment, the desired CO2 concentration was produced as follows. First, the water tank was filled with 6 l deionized water and flushed with gaseous CO2 for approximately one hour. During this time, the conductivity was measured continuously and if the values remain constant, saturation was assumed. This was usually at conductivity values of 40 µS/cm-1. The water tank was filled up with 6 l of CO2-free water and the experimental run started immediately. The water tank was kept closed during the experiment and contained a CO2 headspace. To produce a fully CO2-saturated process water, a similar procedure was applied, but the final dilution was omitted in that case.

steps.title: Prepare ion‑free process water
steps.instruction: Fill a 12 L storage container with deionized water from the Millipore Seralpur Pro 90CN system, confirming conductivity < 0.05 µS cm⁻¹ before use.

steps.title: Adjust CO₂ saturation level
steps.instruction: Set the desired CO₂ content in the process water using a 99.9 % purity CO₂ cylinder and a sintered metal rod for fine gas dispersion.

substeps.instruction: For 50 % CO₂‑saturation: fill the water tank with 6 L deionized water, flush with CO₂ for ~1 h while monitoring conductivity; when conductivity stabilises (≈ 40 µS cm⁻¹) add 6 L CO₂‑free water, start the run immediately, keep the tank closed with a CO₂ headspace.
For fully CO₂‑saturated water: repeat the flushing step but omit the final addition of CO₂‑free water, leaving the 6 L fully saturated water in the tank.

steps.title: Rinse experimental aperture
steps.instruction: Rinse the aperture three times with deionized water to remove residues from previous runs.

steps.title: Load water and incubate
steps.instruction: Pump 6 L of the prepared process water from the bottom up into the aperture to expel trapped air through the upper openings, then let the water stagnate in the aperture for 1 h before starting flow.

steps.title: Start dynamic flow
steps.instruction: Activate the upper pump to draw process water from the 12 L storage tank through the two upper inlet tubings of the POM frame into the recess, distributing it homogeneously into the aperture at the desired flow rate (e.g., 200 ml min⁻¹).

steps.title: Collect samples and measure parameters
steps.instruction: Drain water via the lower openings, collecting samples at intervals based on flow rate (from one sample per 1 L down to one per 0.2 L of discharged water). After each sample, immediately record pH, temperature, and conductivity with a WTW 340i equipped with a TetraCon 325 and a SenTix 41.3 pH electrode, then retain the sample for Ca²⁺ analysis.

steps.title: Continue until equilibrium
steps.instruction: Repeat sampling and measurements until pH and conductivity no longer change, indicating equilibrium has been reached.

steps.title: Terminate experiment
steps.instruction: Switch off the upper pump and allow air to flow into the aperture to empty it, avoiding a pressure drop.
